Order 
Date : 16.05.2024 Heard Mr. S.K. Deuri, learned counsel appearing for the applicants.

Also heard Mr. R.R. Kaushik, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State/respondent No.1 and Mr. S.
Biswas, learned Legal Aid Counsel for the respondent No.2.
2.

This is an application under Section 389(2) Cr.P.C. praying for Page No.# 3/4 granting bail by suspending sentence pending appeal to the applicants in connection with the judgment and order dated 28.07.2022 passed by the learned Assistant Sessions Judge, Diphu, Karbi Anglong, in connection with Sessions Case No. 20/2011, whereby convicting the accused/applicants under Section 376(2)(g) of IPC and sentenced them to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10(ten) years and also to pay fine of Rs.10,000/- each, in default to undergo simple imprisonment for 3(three)
months.
Page No.# 1/4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184811358/
2 3

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicants that the allegation against the applicants is that they had committed rape on the victim girl but the Medical Officer did not find any injury on her private parts.
The learned trial court has failed to appreciate the evidence of other witnesses as well as the victim in proper prospective as such, the decisions of the trial court are perverse.
4. It is also submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that the learned trial court by misreading the evidence on record, convicted the applicants.
It is further submitted that there is every possibility of acquittal of the applicants in the case.
Considering these aspects, the applicants be released on bail during pendency of the appeal.

5. On the other hand, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State has opposed to the prayer of the applicants for suspension of their sentence and has submitted that there is sufficient incriminating materials against the applicants in the record.
As such, bail may not be granted to the applicants during pendency of the appeal.
6. The learned Legal Aid counsel for the respondent No. 2 has Page No.# 4/4 vehemently opposed in granting bail to the applicants during pendency of the appeal.

7. In the case of Ramji Prasad vs Rattan Kumar Jaiswal & Anr; reported in (2002) 9 SCC 366 and in the case of Gomti vs Thakurdas & Ors; reported in (2007) 11 SCC 160, it was held that in heinous crimes like murder, sexual offence etc. proper application of mind to relevant factors and recording of reasons germane to justify grant of bail by the Court, is essential.

sentences.text: 8. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and also gone through the detailed reasons, assigned by the learned trial court, while convicting the accused/applicants in the heinous crime of sexual offence committed towards a girl and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for 10 years.

9. In view of the above, without discussing the evidence in detail and merits of the case, at this stage,
and following the decisions of the Apex Court in Ramji Prasad and Gomti (supra), I do not find it appropriate to release the applicants on bail at this stage.
Accordingly, the prayer of the applicants is rejected.
10. With the above observation, the I/A stands disposed of.
